summary.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

segments.name: Retreading materials (tread rubber, PCTR)
segments.commentary: Management said about 60% of sales come from tread rubber; retread margins were hit by the GST mismatch (18% on retread materials vs 5% on new agricultural tyres), and dealer off-take fell. Industry association has sought a 5% GST rate on retreads, which the government is reportedly considering.

segments.name: Tyres (incl. agricultural, two-wheeler, tractor rear)
segments.commentary: Tyre production rose to 5,35,870 units in FY26 from 3,93,253 in FY25, about 36% growth, while top-line growth lagged. Utilisation in the Indian tyre segment was about 45%. A new heavy-duty tractor rear tyre has received an encouraging dealer response.

segments.name: UAE operations (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; management said margins are better than India, but GCC demand fell from the last quarter of FY26. Utilisation is expected to drop to 30-40% in the near term before recovering to 40-50%. Receivables are rising in the UAE.

segments.name: Exports, precured tyres and US business
segments.commentary: Management said US business started last year and repeat orders are slowly coming in, with a Europe push under way. Logistics are impacted by the Middle East war. No quantified export revenue was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: management expects to at least maintain FY26 levels of performance, and will review this after Q2 FY27 depending on how the situation evolves.
Management expects West Asia and India-related disruptions to normalise by end of Q2 FY27 (pricing, raw material and shipping), which would support better Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margin: management said 10% to 13% is an acceptable range, with a further 2-3% from waste and scrap reduction and operational efficiency.
Management expects a Terra Rubber recycling-linked margin benefit in FY26/FY27 through in-house offtake; no quantified synergy was given.
Management expects capex to be limited this year because existing capacity is sufficient to meet demand, and says the government is likely to correct the GST imbalance.
capex_capacity: Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; the plant has been operating for about 10 years.
Indian utilisation is about 45-55%: retread segment about 55% and tyre segment about 45%.
Gujarat depot commenced operations on December 1, 2025, serving tyre and retread products in Western India.
No significant capex is planned for FY27, as existing capacity is sufficient; cost reduction is focused on automation and AI-based planning tools.
Terra Rubber has started manufacturing and processing scrap into products trialled on road; management is scouting acquisitions but nothing is finalised and no numbers were shared.
demand_pricing: Tyre production volume grew 36% YoY in FY26 (5,35,870 vs 3,93,253 units) and PCTR grew about 10%; bonding gum and flaps grew 56%.
The GST cut on new commercial and agricultural tyres (from 28% to 18% and 5%, respectively) left retread materials at 18%, which narrowed retreading's 30-40% price advantage to about 20%.
Q4 tyre volumes fell QoQ due to dealer off-take hesitancy amid war-related uncertainty in March 2026.
Dealer credit was extended by about one month to 4-5 months, with a stated plan to revert to 3-4 months; China dumping in GCC is extending credit terms up to a year.
Management said competition is intense with tyre majors in retreading materials, but it believes its 40-year expertise gives it an edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was top-line growth only about 12% against the 20% growth previously guided, and how do gross current assets of INR309 crore compare with revenue of INR327 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% was an optimistic projection and that actual growth was about 12%. It pointed to 36% growth in tyre volumes, with the gap explained by selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher tyre production volumes, precured tyres (Europe and the US, where repeat orders are starting), and Terra Rubber integration for in-house raw material offtake.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tyre volumes decline QoQ, and why did working capital rise from about INR230 crore to near INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes fell because of March uncertainty. Working capital is driven by 3-4 months of dealer credit, about 4-5 months of inventory across more than 1,200 SKUs and seasonal rubber prices, and government retentions. IPO proceeds were partly used to fund inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least to maintain FY26 performance and will review after Q2 FY27, preferring to commit less and perform better.

risks_watch: Gross current assets of about INR309 crore versus revenue of INR327 crore indicate high working capital intensity; dealer credit rising to 4-5 months.
The GST mismatch on retread materials (18% vs 5% on new agricultural tyres) is still unresolved; watch the GST Council decision.
UAE utilisation below 50% with receivable risk and China dumping in GCC; management is cautious on aggressive expansion.
Q4 volumes fell QoQ and EBITDA margin declined, so watch whether Q1 FY27 volumes and margins recover.
The Terra Rubber integration and acquisition plans remain unquantified, and no synergy numbers were given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and tyre volumes but cautious on near-term outlook: management repeatedly tied recovery to the West Asia situation and GST policy resolving by Q2 FY27. Evasive on specific numbers, for example declining to commit to FY27 growth and declining to give clear margin guidance.

So we expect similar performance of FY25-'26. So, we believe that it is better to commit less and perform better.
We always try to keep minimum 10% margin, that is a fact, but then due to our efficiency, otherwise our pricing will not be feasible in the market.
We are not taking, not considering any of these options as a priority or low priority, because we are moving in both the verticals.
